Definition: Lowland, i.e. (with the article) the maritime slope of Palestine
BiblicalUsage: The Lowland runs along the coast of the promised land, from the hills down to the sea, and Joshua and the judges fight for it town by town. Deuteronomy names it among the lands Israel must take, and Judah goes down to fight in the valley.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the Lowland is the ground where promise meets resistance, because the valleys are where the chariots live. I hold that God gives the low ground too, and the fight for it is part of the inheritance.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
